exercise.name: Barbell Spider Curl
library_steps: Rest your chest on the steep side of a preacher or incline bench.
Let the bar hang with straight arms, palms up.
Curl the bar up without moving your elbows, then lower it slowly.
exercise.one_line_summary: Chest on a 45 deg incline pad with the armpits over its top edge, a bar hanging in straight arms palms forward; the elbows bend ~125 deg while the upper arms stay vertical. Biceps does the work.

setup.target: Incline ~45 deg, chest on the pad, arms hanging in front of its top edge.
Shoulder width, palms forward and up.

muscles.emg: Main elbow flexor in curls; above 50 % of max RMS in standing and preacher curls.
Active in barbell curls (MARC); library secondary.
muscles.role: Helps bend the elbow, most with the palm turned down.
muscles.surface: Thumb side of the upper forearm.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper arms leave vertical as the bar rises.

sources.citation: Oliveira LF, Matta TT, Alves DS, Garcia MA, Vieira TM. 2009. Effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls. J Sports Sci Med 8(1):24-29.
sources.what_it_gave: Standing, incline and preacher curls: biceps long head above 50 % of max RMS in all; with the upper arm fixed in front (preacher) the biceps worked hardest only over a short early range.

sources.citation: Marcolin G, Panizzolo FA, Petrone N, et al. 2018. Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl. PeerJ 6:e5165.
sources.what_it_gave: Dumbbell, straight-bar and EZ-bar curls at 65 % 1RM: the EZ bar gave higher biceps and brachioradialis EMG than the dumbbell curl; straight vs EZ bar differed little.
